## 1.8.0

_2026-08-12_

The release where `oss` becomes complete on its own — and your repository becomes a pack.

### The rule this release implements
**`oss` ships every capability. An extension supplies only what `oss` cannot know: the tools on your machine, and how your project runs.** A fresh install searches, reads pull requests, follows them, remembers, and runs your project — with nothing else installed.

### New
- **`oss run --pack <dir>`** — the matrix engine now ships inside `oss`. Point it at any directory with a `pack.sh`: your applications, configurations, versions. Nothing is registered. [log4j2-workout](https://github.com/ramanathan1504/log4j2-workout) is the worked example — 19 real applications, and its whole contract is 88 lines.
- **`oss followup`** — the union of both halves that had forked: `--since` (what the author pushed since your review, merges correctly excluded), `--write`, `--comment`, `--changed`, `--mine`, `--record`.
- **`oss hub`** — is anyone waiting on you? Reads only; no send path exists.
- **`oss memory`** — built-in: file, index and search notes with nothing attached. An archive extension still takes over when present, and a working copy stays local so your notes keep improving `pick`.
- **`oss pick`** — what to work on next, scored against what you have already reviewed and written. Reviews count 4× — reviewing something is the one place you demonstrably read the code. Says *why* each suggestion matched.
- **`oss backlog`** — the whole backlog as one page: clusters, mergeable now, one fix away.
- **`oss model`** — the optional 22 MB local model that upgrades search from shared words to shared meaning. Fetched only when you ask.
- **`oss backup` / `restore`** — now covers everything that cannot be re-derived: reviews, memory, vectors, the database, and any attached extension's declared archive. `--to <dir>` targets a synced folder. Verified: 1,152 files out, restored whole onto an empty machine, `pick` and `followup` identical afterwards.

### Fixed
- Backup previously archived only the database — your reviews and notes were silently excluded, and one unreadable iCloud file could abort the walk leaving a partial zip that looked real. Both fixed; skipped files are named, partials are never left behind.
- Every stale `oss-cli <verb>` instruction retired for good.

### Docs
[ubuos.com/docs/connect](https://ubuos.com/docs/connect/) — pack or extension, settled in ten seconds, both halves copyable.

## 1.7.2

_2026-08-12_

**The installed command now starts on macOS 26.** In 1.7.0 and 1.7.1 the bundled runtime crashed at JVM init on macOS 26.5 — every command, immediately. The runtime it ships is now built on JDK 21; what you run is unchanged.

If you hit that crash, `brew upgrade oss` is enough.

### Fixed
- **macOS 26 crash.** The bundled Temurin 17.0.19 runtime died with `SIGSEGV at pc=0` four milliseconds in, before any Java frame. Not the launcher, not jlink, not the jar — that JDK build; a jlink 21 image of the same jar runs fine. The runtime is now 21.
- **The release smoke test could not have caught it**, because it runs on the machine that built the image. That limitation is now written into the workflow rather than rediscovered.
- **Instructions that named a command that no longer exists.** After the rename to `oss`, printed hints still said `oss-cli …` — including the one shown when an extension goes stale. Copying one got `command not found`. `bench` and `kb` in those strings are now `run` and `memory`.
